subject: Post-incident: evidence export, escrow options, and final IR delivery
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dunn <claire.dunn@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Notification: transient telemetry exposure & evidence plan

Claire —

Quick note to let you know we detected a short-lived telemetry replication issue that briefly duplicated request metadata into a non-production analytics bucket. We treated this as an incident and ran containment actions immediately. No customer PII or prompt content was present in the affected records.

What we did (high level):
- Identified replication error at 07:43 PST; isolated pipeline and paused ingestion.
- Rotated the ingestion credentials and removed bucket ACL that caused forward replication.
- Completed a cursory data scan (sanitization rules applied) and confirmed no prompt payload persisted.

Next steps we propose for ClearHealth:
1) Share a sanitized evidence bundle (logs + IR timeline) for your security review.
2) Provide a SIG/SOC2 crosswalk that maps the controls we exercised during containment to the relevant control IDs.
3) Offer an escrow option for a 30-day secure snapshot (SFTP or encrypted Drive) if you need a preserved copy for procurement/audit.

I attached a compact IR timeline and will follow up with a sanitized log package once we complete redaction (should be within 4 business hours). If you have a preferred secure transfer method or an evidence custodian, let me know and we’ll make it happen.

Apologies for the disruption — we know evidence timelines matter for your audit windows.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Customer Security Liaison
Redwood Inference
[attachment: ir_timeline.csv (text/csv)]
From: Claire Dunn <claire.dunn@clearhealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: AuditOps <auditops@clearhealth.com>, procurement@clearhealth.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:02:15 -0800
Subject: Re: Notification: transient telemetry exposure & evidence plan

Thanks Mateo — appreciate the quick heads-up. A few asks from our side so we can align with InfoSec and Procurement: 

- Can you confirm the retention window you propose for the escrow snapshot? We usually request a 90-day hold for incident artifacts during procurement review.
- We need a SIG/CAIQ mapping showing which control IDs were used during containment and any differences compared to our baseline (we’ll feed that to our GRC tool).
- Please include a sanitized syslog extract and a short summary of the redaction rules you applied (fields removed, hashing/scrubbing).

We’d prefer an SFTP drop (preferred) or a password-protected Drive folder; SFTP details will come from procurement once they OK the retention. Can you also provide a point of contact for legal on any evidence-sharing NDA adjustments?

If you can get a preliminary bundle and the SIG mapping today, our team will begin triage and confirm whether we need longer-term escrow.

Best,
Claire Dunn
Security Program Manager
ClearHealth
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dunn <claire.dunn@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 13:30:42 -0800
Subject: Re: Notification: transient telemetry exposure & evidence plan

Claire —

Thanks — short answers and attachments inline.

Retention/escrow:
- Proposal: 30-day standard hold for the live share, extendable to 90 days on request. We generally avoid >90 days without explicit legal/contract terms; happy to discuss escrow contract language.

SIG/CAIQ mapping:
- Attached: sig_control_map.xlsx — column A has SIG control IDs, column B maps to Redwood runbook steps and the artifacts we’re providing.

Sanitization/redaction summary:
- Attached syslog-sanitized-20261102.gz (we: removed IP-level exacts, hashed any candidate identifiers with SHA256, removed full URL query params, and scrubbed user-agent tokens that contained possible identifiers).
- Short redaction note included as the first row in the CSV.

Transfer options & next steps:
- We can SFTP to a host you provide; if procurement prefers Drive we’ll create an AES-256 encrypted folder with password rotated and shared via an out-of-band channel.
- For legal contact: Karthik Iyer (cc’d) is handling evidence sharing agreements and can take a quick Docusign addendum to the existing NDA if needed.

Attachments included in this message: ir_timeline.csv, syslog-sanitized-20261102.gz, sig_control_map.xlsx. We’ll issue a separate secure link to a PDF postmortem within 48 hours.

Let us know SFTP host and retention choice and we’ll start the transfer.

—
Mateo
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dunn <claire.dunn@clearhealth.com>, AuditOps <auditops@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Final: sanitized postmortem & preserved evidence delivery

Claire / Audit team —

Forwarding the finalized post-incident package and summary. Below is the distilled postmortem and the actions we completed; full PDF is attached and the sanitized logs are available at the secure Drive link we shared earlier.

SUMMARY (TL;DR)
- Incident: transient telemetry duplication into non-prod analytics bucket (no customer prompt content).
- Root cause: a misconfigured replication rule combined with a newly deployed transformation that touched the analytics pipeline.
- Impact window: ~07:43–08:01 PST on 2026-11-02.
- Data types affected: telemetry metadata (timestamps, service IDs); no customer prompt or PII according to our redaction scan.

WHAT WE DID
- Containment: paused the replication job, rotated ingestion credentials, removed ACLs, and ran an automated data hygiene job to remove duplicates.
- Remediation: reverted the last transform, tightened CI checks, added a replication rule validator to the deployment gate.
- Audit artifacts delivered: ir_timeline.csv (event-level timeline), syslog-sanitized-20261102.gz (sanitized logs), sig_control_map.xlsx (control crosswalk), postmortem-summary-Redwood-ClearHealth.pdf (formal postmortem).

RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS FOR CLEARHEALTH (suggested)
- Accept the 30-day escrow snapshot now; if procurement requires 90 days, Karthik will prepare an addendum.
- If you want a scoped SOC 2 supplemental snapshot, we can provide token-level audit traces under an MSA amendment.

LOGISTICS & LEGAL
- Per Claire’s note, we prepared an SFTP transfer yesterday to the host details you provided; confirmation shows a successful transfer at 2026-11-03T16:22Z.
- Karthik is ready to route a Docusign addendum for retention >30 days.

If you want a brief 30-minute walkthrough (we can run the sanitized timeline and show the replication rule patch), I can host with Mateo and Karthik this week.

Apologies again; happy to answer any follow-ups.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference
